A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on mathematical reasoning, medical reasoning and figfont puzzles, plus objective ablations and analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds instruction-tuning, coding, multilingual, model-scaling and knowledge-memorization experiments.

M1.justification: The probability-based objective family, power parameterization and hard-thresholding procedure in Equations 1–4 are retained. The additional loss functions discussed in Appendix F are analytical connections, with no corresponding change to the proposed training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds general instruction tuning using Magpie/EvoInstruct and AlpacaEval2, coding using Magicoder and EvalPlus, seven low-resource languages using muri-it and MMLU-ProX, and clean/noisy OpenBookQA knowledge tasks. The original mathematical, medical and puzzle coverage remains.

E2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a numerical reference comparison with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, quoting MBPP/MBPP+ scores of 83.5/71.7 in prose rather than as Table 9 rows. The controlled objective comparisons retain their existing methods; focal, Huber, Dice and GEM losses are discussed without experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce AlpacaEval2 pairwise and length-controlled win rates, EvalPlus pass@1, clean/noisy supervision controls and model scales up to 32B. Appendix C specifies additional corpus sizes, batch sizes and scale-specific learning rates. The previously stated protocols in Appendix B.2 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds within-task model-scaling analyses and an OpenBookQA label-noise robustness experiment. Appendix B.2 also newly reports learning-rate insensitivity over a tuning range. The original quantile-thresholding, objective-convexity and training-likelihood analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing 16-generation averaging for mathematical evaluation and seed-42 disclosures for medical and puzzle evaluation remain. v2 adds no repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–7 retain their numerical values, while Tables 8–11 and Figure 6 add substantial results. Examples include AlpacaEval2 length-controlled win rates of 41.0/49.6/57.5 across 3B/7B/14B, coding averages of 77.8 for -p versus 74.7 for NLL, and noisy OpenBookQA scores of 91.6 versus 27.0 for Qwen2.5-14B. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under existing settings.

T1.justification: The original assumptions, gradient-flow theorem and proofs are retained in renumbered sections. New Appendix F adds mathematical connections to sequence-level RL objectives and derives focal- and Huber-loss gradient weights. Its GEM discussion also introduces an inconsistency: Equation 42's entropy coefficient does not yield Equation 43's stated optimum.

C1.justification: Both versions centrally claim that objective preference depends on model capability: prior-leaning objectives favor strong priors, NLL favors weak priors, and neither consistently dominates between them. v2 makes the absence of a universally superior loss more explicit and expands supporting evidence without redefining that contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix C.5 adds supervision quality as an applicability condition, interpreting NLL's advantage on clean OpenBookQA and -p's robustness under noise. Appendix F adds substantive RL connections and boundaries for composite losses. Meanwhile, v1's explicit caveats about provisional capability measures and limited intermediate-regime exploration are removed rather than relocated.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses the learning-rate search grid and documents additional dataset filtering, sampling, training budgets, batch sizes and learning rates in Appendix C. The existing framework, hardware and code-access information remain. Reproducibility is still incomplete for the new OpenBookQA experiment because the noise rate and perturbation procedure are unspecified.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix F substantially expand positioning against alternative losses and RL objectives, including newly cited work by Davis and Recht, Rege Cambrin et al., and Li et al. Much of the RL-inspired SFT discussion already appeared in v1's Appendix A; the substantive expansion concerns additional loss families and their relationship to the continuum.

P1.justification: Most original prose and section ordering survive. v2 revises the abstract and introduction, inserts a main-text related-work overview, shortens the conclusion and reorganizes the appendices, including removing the standalone limitations section and adding a literature discussion.

P2.justification: v2 converts the main text and references to two columns, restyles retained tables with colored objective rows, and resizes existing plots. It adds Figures 3 and 6 and Tables 8–11. The original quantile and convexity/likelihood figures become Figures 4 and 5, preserving their analyses.

improvement.justification: The new within-task scale studies and low-resource-language evaluations strengthen support for the continuum beyond v1's separation into three task domains. However, the unspecified OpenBookQA corruption procedure, removal of capability-measure caveats, and inconsistency in the new GEM equations temper these empirical gains and limit the net quality improvement.
